events.title: Early Human Settlement
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows modern humans inhabited the Algerian region for over 200,000 years. Rock art and tools found in the Sahara prove the existence of early hunter-gatherer societies. These early inhabitants were ancestors of the indigenous Berber peoples of North Africa.

events.title: Neolithic Culture
events.description: The Sahara region had a more humid climate supporting agriculture and pastoralism. Tassili rock art depicts this period's lifestyle including cattle herds, hunting scenes, and religious rituals. This was an important stage in North African civilization development.

events.title: Green Sahara Period
events.description: Sahara region entered warm humid period with grasslands and lakes widespread, supporting large populations and wildlife. Archaeological evidence shows complex hunter-gatherer societies developing, using pottery and polished stone tools. This period laid foundation for later civilization development.

events.title: Early Pastoralism
events.description: North African region began domesticating cattle and sheep, transitioning from hunting-gathering to pastoralism. Tassili rock art clearly depicts herds and pastoral life, showing flourishing pastoral culture. This marked major shift in economic mode.

events.title: Sahara Rock Art Peak
events.description: Rock art in Tassili Plateau and Ahaggar Mountains reached artistic peak, depicting rich wildlife, hunting scenes and religious rituals. These paintings became important sources for studying prehistoric North African culture, showing Sahara region's ecological diversity.

events.title: Late Rock Art Style
events.description: Sahara rock art entered late phase, style shifting from realistic to abstract and symbolic. Depicted content reflects climate change and social transformation, including appearance of horses and chariots, showing contact with Mediterranean world.

events.title: Sahara Desertification
events.description: Climate change caused gradual desertification of the Sahara region, forcing population migration north to Mediterranean coast and south to Sahel region. This change shaped North Africa's population distribution patterns and promoted coastal area development.

events.title: Bronze Age Technology
events.description: North African region began using bronze tools and weapons, marking technological progress. Archaeological discoveries show trade connections with eastern Mediterranean and sub-Saharan Africa. This period witnessed more complex social organization and specialized craftsmanship development.

events.title: Berber Kingdom Formation
events.description: Berbers established multiple tribal confederations and small kingdoms, including ancestors of Numidians. These societies developed complex political structures, trade networks, and military organizations. Berbers were renowned for their cavalry, becoming important force in Mediterranean world.

events.title: Phoenician Trade Contact
events.description: Phoenician merchants began exploring North African coast, seeking precious metals and trade opportunities. They established initial contacts with Berber tribes, exchanging Mediterranean goods for local resources. These early contacts laid foundation for later colonization.

events.title: Phoenician Arrival
events.description: Phoenicians established trading posts along North African coast, including site that became Carthage. They built trade relationships with local Berbers, introducing new technologies, writing systems, and Mediterranean trade networks.

events.title: Carthaginian Expansion
events.description: Carthaginian Empire extended its influence to Algerian coastal regions, establishing multiple colonies and trading posts. Carthaginians formed alliances with Berber tribes to jointly resist Roman expansion. This period witnessed deep integration of North Africa with Mediterranean world.

events.title: Berber Script Development
events.description: Ancient Berbers developed Tifinagh script for recording language and commercial transactions. This writing system was widely used in Sahara region, becoming important symbol of Berber cultural identity, still used among Tuareg people today.

events.title: Numidian Kingdom Rise
events.description: Berbers established powerful Numidian Kingdom, renowned for excellent cavalry. Numidia played key role in Punic Wars, supporting both Carthage and Rome at different times. King Massinissa unified Numidian tribes, establishing lasting kingdom.

events.title: Second Punic War
events.description: Numidian cavalry played important role in Hannibal's war against Rome. Massinissa initially supported Carthage, then switched to Rome, becoming key factor in Battle of Zama. This choice brought territorial expansion and Roman support to Numidia.

events.title: Massinissa's Reign
events.description: King Massinissa ruled Numidia for nearly 60 years, establishing powerful and stable kingdom. He promoted agricultural development, urbanization, and absorption of Greco-Roman culture. Numidia became North Africa's most powerful independent kingdom, capital Cirta (modern Constantine) flourished.

events.title: Fall of Carthage and Roman Rule Begins
events.description: After Third Punic War Carthage was destroyed by Rome, Romans began direct rule of North Africa. Numidian Kingdom split, parts became Roman provinces. Romans built new cities, roads and infrastructure, introducing Roman law and administrative systems.

events.title: Jugurthine War
events.description: Numidian King Jugurtha fought prolonged war with Rome. Jugurtha employed guerrilla tactics and bribed Roman officials, resisting stubbornly. War ended with Jugurtha betrayed to Rome by Mauritanian King Bocchus, marking decline of Numidian independence.

events.title: Roman Province Established
events.description: Emperor Augustus formally organized Algerian region as province of Mauretania Caesariensis, with capital at Caesarea (modern Cherchell). Roman rule brought urbanization, Christianity spread and Latin cultural influence.

events.title: Fall of Mauretanian Kingdom
events.description: Roman Emperor Caligula executed Mauretanian King Ptolemy, formally ending last independent Berber kingdom. Rome divided region into two provinces: Mauretania Tingitana and Mauretania Caesariensis.

events.title: Foundation of Timgad
events.description: Emperor Trajan established Timgad city on Sahara edge as military colony. This city built following perfect Roman grid plan, equipped with theater, baths, library and other facilities, showcasing pinnacle of Roman urban planning.

events.title: Romanization and Prosperity
events.description: Algeria experienced golden age under Roman rule. Many cities built like Timgad, Djemila, developing agriculture and trade. Berbers gradually Romanized, many gained Roman citizenship. Christianity began spreading.

events.title: Septimius Severus Rise
events.description: Septimius Severus from North African Leptis became Roman Emperor, founding Severan Dynasty. His rule demonstrated North African elite's importance in Roman Empire politics, strengthening investment and defense in North Africa.

events.title: Saint Perpetua's Martyrdom
events.description: Christian martyrs Perpetua and Felicitas executed in Carthage, their martyrdom account becoming one of early Christianity's most important documents. This event inspired spread of North African Christianity.

events.title: Gordian Revolt
events.description: North African Governor Gordian I launched revolt against Roman Emperor Maximinus at Thysdrus (modern Tunisia), declaring himself emperor. Though revolt failed, it showed North Africa's important position in Roman Empire politics.

events.title: Domitius Revolt
events.description: Berber tribal leader Domitius launched large-scale uprising in Mauretania against Roman rule. Revolt lasted several years, forcing Rome to deploy large armies for suppression, showing Berber resistance to Romanization.

events.title: Rise of Christianity and Donatism
events.description: Christianity spread rapidly in North Africa, producing important theologians like Saint Augustine. Donatist Christianity particularly strong in Algeria, conflicting with orthodox Christianity. Period also witnessed Berber uprisings against Roman rule.

events.title: Firmus Revolt
events.description: Berber chieftain Firmus launched uprising in Mauretania, supported by Donatist Christians. Rome sent famous general Theodosius (later emperor) to suppress it, revolt ultimately failed but had lasting impact.

events.title: Gildo Revolt
events.description: African Governor Gildo declared independence from Western Roman Empire, aligning with Eastern Roman Empire. This revolt reflected impact of Roman Empire division on North Africa and local elite political ambitions.

events.title: Vandal Kingdom
events.description: Germanic Vandals under Genseric conquered North Africa, establishing Vandal Kingdom with capital at Carthage. Vandals controlled western Mediterranean, competing with Byzantine Empire for naval supremacy. They practiced Arian Christianity, persecuting orthodox Christians.

events.title: Byzantine Reconquest
events.description: Byzantine Emperor Justinian I sent Belisarius to reconquer North Africa, ending Vandal rule. Byzantine rule restored orthodox Christianity but faced continuous Berber resistance. Byzantine control mainly limited to coastal cities and fortresses.

events.title: Arab Conquest
events.description: Arab Muslim armies under Uqba ibn Nafi conquered North Africa. Berber queen Kahina led resistance but ultimately failed. Arabs established Kairouan as North African Islamic rule center, beginning large-scale Islamization and Arabization process.

events.title: Battle of Sufetula
events.description: Arab armies defeated Byzantine forces at Sufetula, Governor Gregory killed in battle. This was key battle in Arab conquest of North Africa, laying foundation for subsequent Islamization.

events.title: Kahina Resistance
events.description: Berber Queen Kahina (Dihya) led Aurès Mountain tribes resisting Arab conquest. Called 'Berber Prophetess,' she successfully resisted for years before dying in battle, becoming symbol of Berber resistance.

events.title: Great Berber Revolt
events.description: North African Berbers launched large-scale uprising against Umayyad Caliphate rule and Arab privileged status. Revolt adopted Kharijite doctrine demanding equality and justice, nearly overthrowing Arab rule.

events.title: Rustamid Dynasty Established
events.description: Persian-descended Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam established Rustamid dynasty at Tahert, following Kharijite Islam. Dynasty became symbol of Berber independence, promoting trade and scholarly development.

events.title: Aghlabid Dynasty Rise
events.description: Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab established Aghlabid dynasty in Ifriqiya (modern Tunisia and eastern Algeria), nominally loyal to Abbasid Caliphate but effectively independent. Dynasty promoted agricultural, trade and architectural development, Kairouan became important cultural center.

events.title: Islamization and Berber Revolts
events.description: Berbers gradually converted to Islam but maintained many traditional customs. Kharijite Islam popular among Berbers, leading to multiple revolts against Umayyad and Abbasid Caliphates. Rustamid dynasty established independent Kharijite state at Tahert.

events.title: Fatimid Conquest
events.description: Shia Ismaili missionaries established Fatimid dynasty, overthrowing Aghlabids. Fatimids claimed caliphate title, challenging Abbasid authority. They established Mahdia as capital, beginning rule over North Africa.

events.title: Fatimid Dynasty Rule
events.description: Shia Fatimid dynasty conquered North Africa with capital at Mahdia. Fatimids later moved capital to Cairo, leaving Zirid dynasty as their representatives in North Africa. Period witnessed trade prosperity and cultural development, but also continuous Berber tribal unrest.

events.title: Hammadid Dynasty Established
events.description: Hammad ibn Buluggin established Hammadid dynasty at Qal'a, breaking away from Zirid dynasty independence. Dynasty controlled central Algeria, renowned for military strength and architectural achievements.

events.title: Almoravid and Almohad Dynasties
events.description: Berber Almoravid dynasty from Morocco unified Maghreb, later replaced by Almohad dynasty. Almohads established strong rule in Algeria, promoting Islamic scholarship and architectural development. Tlemcen became important scholarly and commercial center.

events.title: Almohad Conquest
events.description: Almohad Caliph Abd al-Mu'min conquered Algeria, ending Hammadid dynasty rule. Almohad dynasty unified entire Maghreb, implementing strict Islamic reforms.

events.title: Zayyanid Dynasty Established
events.description: Yaghmurasen ibn Zyan established Zayyanid dynasty (Abd al-Wadid) at Tlemcen, controlling central-western Algeria. Dynasty had complex relationships with Granada, Marinids and Hafsids.

events.title: Local Dynasty Division
events.description: After Almohad decline, Algeria split into multiple local dynasties: Zayyanid dynasty controlled Tlemcen, Hafsid dynasty controlled east. These dynasties had complex diplomatic relations with Granada, Marinids and Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Spanish Occupation of Oran
events.description: Spanish Cardinal Jiménez led forces occupying Oran, establishing fortress to control this port. This was part of Spanish expansion in North Africa, threatening local Muslim rulers.

events.title: Ottoman Brothers Arrive
events.description: Turkish corsair brothers Aruj and Hayreddin Barbarossa invited to help Algiers against Spain. After Aruj killed, Hayreddin became Algiers ruler, seeking Ottoman Empire protection, beginning Ottoman rule era.

events.title: Death of Aruj
events.description: Turkish corsair Aruj killed by Spanish forces at Tlemcen. His brother Hayreddin inherited his enterprise, later becoming famous Barbarossa, establishing Ottoman rule in North Africa.

events.title: Ottoman Algeria Established
events.description: Hayreddin Barbarossa formally placed Algiers under Ottoman Sultan rule, becoming Ottoman Empire province. Algiers developed as powerful corsair base and Mediterranean trade center, Janissary corps became ruling class.

events.title: Charles V Expedition Failure
events.description: Holy Roman Emperor Charles V personally led large army attacking Algiers but failed due to storms and fierce resistance. This failure consolidated Ottoman position in western Mediterranean.

events.title: Morisco Immigration Wave
events.description: After Spain expelled Moriscos (Muslim descendants), large numbers of refugees flooded into Algeria. These immigrants brought advanced agricultural techniques, crafts and architectural knowledge, enriching Algeria's culture and economy.

events.title: Barbary Corsair Golden Age
events.description: Algiers became main Barbary corsair base, raiding European merchant ships and enslaving Christians. Corsair activities brought enormous wealth to Algiers, supporting urban development and military power. European nations repeatedly attempted to conquer Algiers but all failed.

events.title: Dey Rule Established
events.description: Janissary corps overthrew Pasha rule, establishing Dey system. Dey became Algeria's actual ruler, though nominally still belonging to Ottoman Empire. This system lasted until French conquest, Deys elected through Janissary council.

events.title: French Naval Bombardment of Algiers
events.description: French Admiral Duquesne led fleet twice bombarding Algiers, attempting to force Dey to stop corsair activities and release French slaves. Though causing enormous destruction, failed to achieve objectives, showing Algiers' stubborn resistance.

events.title: Dey Baba Ali Rule
events.description: Baba Ali became Algiers Dey, ruling for 25 years. He strengthened corsair activities, engaged in complex diplomatic games with European nations, bringing Algiers to power peak.

events.title: Spanish Expedition to Algiers
events.description: Spanish King Charles III sent large army attacking Algiers but suffered devastating defeat. This was 18th century Europe's largest military action against Algiers, failure further enhanced Algiers' prestige.

events.title: US-Algiers War
events.description: US Navy defeated Algiers corsairs in Second Barbary War, forcing Dey to sign treaty stopping attacks on American ships. This marked decline of Barbary corsair power and strengthening European influence in North Africa.

events.title: British Fleet Bombards Algiers
events.description: British Admiral Edward Pellew led fleet bombarding Algiers, forcing Dey to release Christian slaves and sign treaty. This marked decisive European naval victory over Barbary corsairs.

events.title: French Debt Dispute
events.description: Dispute arose between France and Algiers Dey over wheat supply debt. Two Jewish merchants Bacri brothers involved, becoming catalyst for deteriorating relations. This economic dispute eventually evolved into 1827 Fan Incident.

events.title: Fan Incident
events.description: Algiers Dey Hussein struck French consul with fan during dispute, becoming pretext for French invasion. This seemingly trivial incident triggered diplomatic crisis leading to French conquest of Algeria.

events.title: French Conquest of Algiers
events.description: French forces landed at Sidi Ferruch, after three-week siege occupied Algiers. Dey Hussein surrendered and went into exile, ending Ottoman rule. France initially claimed only punitive expedition but soon decided permanent occupation.

events.title: Abd al-Qadir Resistance
events.description: Young religious leader Abd al-Qadir organized resistance to French occupation in western Algeria. He established modernized Arab state, conducting 15-year guerrilla war. Finally surrendered in 1847 but became Algerian national hero.

events.title: Abd al-Qadir State Building
events.description: Abd al-Qadir established modernized Arab state at Mascara, drafting constitution, building army and administrative institutions. His state became important force resisting French colonial rule.

events.title: Battle of Iron Gates
events.description: French forces defeated Abd al-Qadir's army at Iron Gates, marking turning point in Algerian War. French adopted scorched earth tactics, destroying crops and villages, forcing Arab tribes to surrender.

events.title: Algeria Becomes French Territory
events.description: France formally incorporated Algeria into French mainland, dividing into three provinces: Algiers, Oran and Constantine. Began large-scale European immigration program, establishing colonial farms and cities. Indigenous people stripped of land and political rights.

events.title: Kabylia Conquest
events.description: French forces completed conquest of Kabylia mountains, Algeria's last independent region. During conquest French used brutal methods including cave smoking tactics.

events.title: Arab Kingdom Project
events.description: Napoleon III attempted to establish 'Arab Kingdom' giving Muslims more rights to balance settler power. But policy faced strong settler opposition and was abandoned after Second Empire's collapse in 1870.

events.title: Senatus-Consulte Decree
events.description: Napoleon III issued decree theoretically allowing Muslims to apply for French citizenship, on condition of abandoning Islamic legal status. Very few accepted this condition, showing failure of French assimilation policy.

events.title: Crémieux Decree
events.description: France issued Crémieux Decree granting Algerian Jews French citizenship while excluding Muslims. This policy intensified religious and racial tensions with lasting impact.

events.title: Great Kabylia Uprising
events.description: Mohamed Mokrani led large-scale Kabylia Berber uprising protesting French colonial rule and land confiscation. Uprising spread to most of Algeria but ultimately suppressed by French forces. France imposed collective punishment, confiscating more land for European settlers.

events.title: Laveigerie Law
events.description: French Parliament passed law transferring Algeria's administrative management from military to civilian control. This strengthened European settlers' political power but further marginalized Muslim population.

events.title: Indigenous Code Implementation
events.description: France enacted discriminatory Indigenous Code, stripping Algerian Muslims of civil rights. Muslims treated as French subjects not citizens, subject to special courts with restricted movement. This system reinforced colonial racial segregation.

events.title: Anti-Jewish Riots in Oran and Algiers
events.description: Economic difficulties and resentment from Crémieux Decree triggered anti-Jewish violence. European settlers attacked Jewish communities, reflecting ethnic tensions within colonial society.

events.title: Colonial Economic Boom
events.description: Algerian wine industry flourished, becoming one of France's largest wine exporters. European settlers established large farms growing grapes, citrus fruits and grains. Colonial economic development further dispossessed Arab and Berber farmers of their land.

events.title: Young Algerians Movement
events.description: Inspired by Turkish Young Turks, Algerian intellectuals launched Young Algerians movement demanding political reforms and equal rights. This was early expression of modern Algerian nationalism.

events.title: World War I
events.description: About 170,000 Algerians conscripted into French army, approximately 25,000 died in war. Algerians expected more rights after war, but France failed to deliver on promises, deepening resentment.

events.title: Post-War Reform Disappointment
events.description: After WWI France failed to fulfill promises to Algerian Muslim veterans. Jonnart-Morinaud reform proposal rejected by settlers, deepening disappointment among Muslim intellectuals and promoting nationalist movement development.

events.title: Nationalist Movement Rise
events.description: After WWI, Algerian nationalist movement emerged. Messali Hadj founded North African Star demanding independence. Moderates like Ferhat Abbas sought assimilation and equal rights. Islamic reform movement also promoted national consciousness awakening.

events.title: North African Star Founded
events.description: Messali Hadj founded North African Star organization in Paris, first political organization explicitly demanding Algerian independence. Organization later developed into Algerian People's Party.

events.title: Colonial Centenary Celebrations
events.description: France held grand celebrations commemorating 100 years of Algerian conquest, triggering strong protests from Algerian nationalists. Celebrations showcased colonial achievements but also stimulated anti-colonial movement development.

events.title: Association of Ulema Founded
events.description: Abd al-Hamid Ben Badis founded Association of Algerian Muslim Ulema, promoting Islamic educational reform and Arabic revival. Association's slogan 'Islam is our religion, Arabic is our language, Algeria is our homeland' became important expression of national identity.

events.title: Blum-Violette Plan
events.description: French Popular Front government proposed Blum-Violette Plan to grant French citizenship to some Algerian Muslims. But faced strong settler opposition, plan ultimately failed, greatly disappointing moderate nationalists.

events.title: Operation Torch
events.description: Allied forces landed in Algeria launching Operation Torch. Algiers became provisional capital of Free France, with de Gaulle establishing government-in-exile. North African campaign made Algeria important strategic base.

events.title: Algerian People's Manifesto
events.description: Ferhat Abbas issued 'Algerian People's Manifesto' demanding establishment of Algerian Republic. This was first time moderate nationalists explicitly demanded independence.

events.title: Brazzaville Conference
events.description: De Gaulle convened Brazzaville Conference to discuss French colonies' future, but rejected any independence possibility. After conference announced limited reforms allowing some Muslims voting rights, but far from satisfying nationalist demands.

events.title: Setif Massacre
events.description: During VE Day celebrations, Algerian demands for independence triggered conflicts. French forces and settlers massacred Muslims, death toll estimated at tens of thousands. This event intensified Algerian anti-French sentiment, laying groundwork for independence war.

events.title: Second Constituent Assembly
events.description: Ferhat Abbas elected as French Constituent Assembly representative, promoting Algerian reforms. Proposed bill granting Muslims equal rights but faced fierce settler opposition and failed.

events.title: Algeria Statute
events.description: French Parliament passed Algeria Statute promising political reforms and local assembly establishment. But statute implementation riddled with electoral fraud, Muslim representation systematically weakened, reforms became nominal.

events.title: Secret Organization Founded
events.description: Radical nationalists established Secret Organization (OS) beginning preparations for armed struggle. Organization broken by French police but survivors later became FLN core. This marked turning point from peaceful protest to armed struggle.

events.title: Algerian War Begins
events.description: National Liberation Front (FLN) launched armed uprising, marking beginning of Algerian War of Independence. Uprising erupted simultaneously nationwide, FLN issued declaration demanding complete independence. France sent large army to suppress, war lasted eight years.

events.title: Philippeville Massacre
events.description: August 20, Algerian nationalists launched attacks at Philippeville, French forces and settlers conducted retaliatory massacre. This event marked Algerian War entering more bloody phase.

events.title: Battle of Algiers
events.description: FLN launched urban guerrilla warfare in Algiers city, French forces implemented harsh repression including torture. This battle became typical case of modern anti-colonial warfare, attracting international attention. French military victory but political failure.

events.title: Sakiet Sidi Youssef Bombing
events.description: French air force bombed Sakiet Sidi Youssef village on Tunisian border, causing massive civilian casualties. This incident drew international condemnation, damaging France's international image.

events.title: French Political Crisis and de Gaulle's Return
events.description: Algerian French settlers and military staged coup demanding de Gaulle's return to power. De Gaulle returned establishing Fifth Republic, initially supporting 'French Algeria' but gradually shifting toward Algerian self-determination.

events.title: Algiers Barricades Week
events.description: January 24 to February 1, Algiers Europeans built barricades opposing de Gaulle's self-determination policy. This event showed deep divisions between settlers and French mainland government.

events.title: Secret Army Organization (OAS) Terror
events.description: Extremist settlers and officers formed Secret Army Organization opposing de Gaulle's Algeria policy. OAS conducted terrorist attacks in Algeria and mainland France, even attempting to assassinate de Gaulle. Their extremism actually accelerated independence process.

events.title: Generals' Putsch
events.description: Four French generals staged coup in Algiers opposing de Gaulle's Algeria policy. After coup failed, extremist settlers formed OAS continuing resistance.

events.title: Great Migration
events.description: Before and after Algerian independence, about 1 million European settlers (pieds-noirs) and pro-French Muslims (harkis) fled Algeria. This great migration changed Algeria's demographic structure.

events.title: Algerian Independence
events.description: After referendum, Algeria formally declared independence, ending 132 years of French colonial rule. Ahmed Ben Bella became first president. About 1 million European settlers (pieds-noirs) fled Algeria, causing massive brain drain and capital flight.

events.title: Evian Accords
events.description: France and FLN signed Evian Accords ending Algerian War. Agreement stipulated ceasefire, self-determination referendum, protection of European rights. This marked France's recognition of Algeria's inevitable independence.

events.title: Sand War
events.description: Algeria and Morocco fought armed conflict over border disputes, mainly in Tindouf and Bechar regions. Conflict eventually resolved through Organization of African Unity mediation.

events.title: Boumediene Coup
events.description: Defense Minister Houari Boumediene staged military coup overthrowing Ben Bella government. Boumediene established military dictatorship, pursuing socialist policies and Arabization process. He ruled 19 years until death in 1978.

events.title: Six-Day War Stance
events.description: Algeria firmly supported Arab states in Six-Day War, breaking relations with Israel. Boumediene government positioned Algeria as leader of Third World and Arab world.

events.title: Oil Boom and Industrialization
events.description: Oil crisis greatly increased Algeria's oil revenues, Boumediene government pursued ambitious industrialization program. Built heavy industry, petrochemicals, but neglected agriculture and light industry. Oil revenues also used to support Third World liberation movements.

events.title: Western Sahara Issue
events.description: After Spanish withdrawal from Western Sahara, Algeria supported Polisario Front independence struggle, creating long-term confrontation with Morocco. This issue still affects Maghreb regional relations today.

events.title: Chadli Bendjedid Takes Power
events.description: After Boumediene's death, Chadli Bendjedid became president. He pursued economic liberalization policies but also faced serious economic and social problems.

events.title: Berber Spring
events.description: Kabylia region erupted in Berber protests demanding recognition of Berber language and culture. Government suppressed protests but Berber cultural movement continued developing. This marked beginning of Algeria's multicultural identity issues.

events.title: Oil Price Collapse
events.description: International oil prices plummeted, Algeria's economy severely damaged. Government forced to implement austerity policies, cutting subsidies, triggering social discontent.

events.title: October Riots
events.description: Economic crisis triggered nationwide riots, people protesting food shortages, unemployment and corruption. Government declared martial law, army opened fire killing hundreds. Riots forced government to undertake political reforms, ending one-party system.

events.title: New Constitution and Multi-party System
events.description: Algeria adopted new constitution allowing multi-party system and press freedom. Opposition parties like Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) established. This marked Algeria's attempted transition from one-party to pluralistic politics.

events.title: Local Elections
events.description: Algeria held first multi-party local elections, Islamic Salvation Front won overwhelming victory. This result shocked secularists and military, laying groundwork for later political crisis.

events.title: Election Interruption and Military Intervention
events.description: In first multi-party elections, Islamic Salvation Front led first round voting. Military fearing Islamist victory forced President Chadli Bendjedid to resign, cancelled second round elections, triggering political crisis.

events.title: Algerian Civil War (Black Decade)
events.description: After military cancelled elections, Islamic armed groups launched rebellion, Algeria plunged into bloody civil war. Government forces battled Islamic Armed Group (GIA) and others, massive civilian casualties. Estimated 200,000 deaths, called 'Black Decade'.

events.title: Liamine Zéroual Takes Office
events.description: Retired General Liamine Zéroual became president, promising to end civil war. He pursued 'eradication' policy, severely cracking down on Islamic militants.

events.title: Rais Massacre
events.description: August 29, militants massacred about 400 civilians in Rais village near Algiers. This was one of bloodiest events during civil war, shocking international community.

events.title: Bouteflika Elected President
events.description: Abdelaziz Bouteflika elected president promising to end civil war. He pursued 'national reconciliation' policy, offering amnesty to Islamic militants. Civil war gradually subsided but national trauma remained deep.

events.title: Kabylia Black Spring
events.description: Death of Berber youth in police custody triggered massive Kabylia protests. Demonstrators demanded recognition of Berber as official language, withdrawal of gendarmerie. Government eventually recognized Tamazight (Berber) as national language.

events.title: National Reconciliation Charter
events.description: Algeria passed National Reconciliation Charter referendum, providing amnesty for violence during civil war. Charter aimed at achieving national reconciliation but also sparked controversy.

events.title: Arab Spring Impact
events.description: Inspired by Arab Spring, Algeria saw protest activities but limited scale. Government quickly raised subsidies and wages, promised political reforms. Due to fresh civil war memories, people were cautious about political upheaval.

events.title: Bouteflika Fourth Term
events.description: Despite poor health, Bouteflika still elected for fourth presidential term. His rule increasingly relied on military and intelligence services, corruption problems became increasingly serious.

events.title: Constitutional Amendment
events.description: Algeria passed constitutional amendment recognizing Tamazight as official language, limiting presidential terms. But critics considered reform insufficient.

events.title: Tebboune Elected President
events.description: Abdelmadjid Tebboune elected president in controversial election with historically low turnout. Protesters boycotted election demanding complete political system change. Tebboune promised reforms but faced legitimacy crisis.

events.title: Bouteflika Resignation
events.description: Facing continuous protests and military pressure, President Bouteflika who ruled 20 years announced resignation. This marked major change in Algeria's political system, but protesters demanded deeper institutional reforms.

events.title: Smile Revolution Begins
events.description: Bouteflika's announcement of fifth presidential term candidacy triggered nationwide massive peaceful protests. People demanded political change and anti-corruption, protest movement called 'Smile Revolution' or 'Hirak' movement.

events.title: COVID-19 and Protest Suspension
events.description: COVID pandemic forced Hirak protest movement suspension, government used opportunity to consolidate power. Economy deteriorated due to oil price collapse and pandemic impact. Government arrested many activists and journalists, raising human rights concerns.

events.title: Breaking Relations with Morocco
events.description: Algeria broke diplomatic relations with Morocco over Western Sahara issue and other disputes. Deteriorating relations between two countries affected entire Maghreb regional cooperation.

events.title: Ongoing Challenges
events.description: Algeria faces multiple challenges: economy over-dependent on oil, high youth unemployment, stagnant political reforms. Hirak movement reduced in scale but still exists. Government struggles between maintaining stability and meeting reform demands. Regional security threats and climate change also major challenges.
